ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Twelve congruent disks are placed on a circle $C$ of radius 1 in such a way that the twelve disks cover $C$, no two of the disks overlap, and so that each of the twelve disks is tangent to its two neighbors. The resulting arrangement of disks is shown in the figure below. The sum of the areas of the twelve disks can be written in the from $\pi(a-b\sqrt{c})$, where $a,b,c$ are positive integers and $c$ is not divisible by the square of any prime. Find $a+b+c$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has a large circle C with radius labeled 1, and 12 congruent small disks are evenly arranged near the circumference. On the large circle C, 12 black points are marked; from the figure it can be seen that these black points are evenly distributed along the large circle and correspond to the contact positions of adjacent small disks. Each small disk covers an arc between two adjacent black points on the large circle C, and each small disk is tangent only to its left and right adjacent small disks, with no mutual overlap. Reasoning: Since there are 12 congruent disks covering circle C in the 12-fold symmetric manner shown in the figure, the central angle corresponding to adjacent black points on circle C is 2π/12 = π/6. Let the adjacent two black points be P,Q, the center of the large circle be O, the center of the small disk covering arc PQ be S, and the radius of the small disk be r. Let φ = π/12. Then OS lies on the perpendicular bisector of chord PQ, so ∠POS = φ. Let x = OS. Since OP = 1 and SP = r, by the law of cosines, r^2 = x^2 + 1 - 2x cos φ. The center of the adjacent small disk can be obtained by rotating S around O by π/6, so the distance between the centers of two adjacent small disks is 2x sin φ. Adjacent small disks are tangent, so this distance equals 2r, that is, r = x sin φ. Substituting into r^2 = x^2 + 1 - 2x cos φ gives x^2 sin^2 φ = x^2 + 1 - 2x cos φ. Simplifying gives x^2 cos^2 φ - 2x cos φ + 1 = 0, namely (x cos φ - 1)^2 = 0, so x = sec φ, r = x sin φ = tan φ = tan(π/12) = tan 15°. Therefore the total area is 12πr^2 = 12π tan^2 15°. Also tan 15° = 2 - √3, so tan^2 15° = (2 - √3)^2 = 7 - 4√3. The total area is 12π(7 - 4√3) = π(84 - 48√3). Thus a = 84, b = 48, c = 3, and a+b+c = 135.

Since 12 congruent disks appear cyclically, the 12 tangency points divide C into arcs of 30°, so for one disk covering the arc from P to Q, the midpoint direction OS makes angle 15° with OP. raw_record.original_question: Twelve congruent disks are placed on a circle $C$ of radius 1 in such a way that the twelve disks cover $C$, no two of the disks overlap, and each of the twelve disks is tangent to its two neighbors. The resulting arrangement of disks is shown in the figure. The sum of the areas of the twelve disks can be written in the form $\pi(a-b\sqrt{c})$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive integers and $c$ is not divisible by the square of any prime. Find $a+b+c$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure has a large circle C with radius labeled 1, and 12 congruent small disks are evenly arranged near the circumference. On the large circle C, 12 black points are marked; from the figure it can be seen that these black points are evenly distributed along the large circle and correspond to the contact positions of adjacent small disks. Each small disk covers an arc between two adjacent black points on the large circle C, and each small disk is tangent only to its left and right adjacent small disks, with no mutual overlap.

Reasoning: Since there are 12 congruent disks covering circle C in the 12-fold symmetric manner shown in the figure, the central angle corresponding to adjacent black points on circle C is 2π/12 = π/6. Let the adjacent two black points be P,Q, the center of the large circle be O, the center of the small disk covering arc PQ be S, and the radius of the small disk be r. Let φ = π/12; let x = OS. Then OS lies on the perpendicular bisector of chord PQ, so ∠POS = φ. Since OP = 1 and SP = r, by the law of cosines, r^2 = x^2 + 1 - 2x cos φ. The center of the adjacent small disk can be obtained by rotating S around O by π/6, so the distance between the centers of two adjacent small disks is 2x sin φ. Adjacent small disks are tangent, so this distance equals 2r, that is, r = x sin φ. Substituting into r^2 = x^2 + 1 - 2x cos φ gives x^2 sin^2 φ = x^2 + 1 - 2x cos φ. Simplifying gives x^2 cos^2 φ - 2x cos φ + 1 = 0, namely (x cos φ - 1)^2 = 0, so x = sec φ, r = x sin φ = tan φ = tan(π/12) = tan 15°. Therefore the total area is 12πr^2 = 12π tan^2 15°. Also tan 15° = 2 - √3, so tan^2 15° = (2 - √3)^2 = 7 - 4√3. The total area is 12π(7 - 4√3) = π(84 - 48√3). Thus a = 84, b = 48, c = 3, and a+b+c = 135.
